🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Chilean filmmaker Sebastián Lelio, the Oscar-winning director of A Fantastic Woman, has died at 52.

Lelio died on Friday, November 6, 2026, at his home in the Las Condes neighborhood of Santiago, Chile. His family confirmed his death in a statement shared by his partner, actress Amalia Kassai, saying he died "for health reasons." No specific cause was given. The family asked for respect for their privacy, saying, "We are going through a moment of great pain and his memory will remain forever among us."

Born on March 8, 1974, in Mendoza, Argentina, Lelio moved to Chile with his mother at the age of two and studied at the Film School of Chile. He became one of the most acclaimed voices in Latin American cinema, known for films centered on characters who defy prejudice and convention.

His breakthrough came with Gloria (2013), which won Paulina García the Silver Bear for Best Actress at the Berlin Film Festival. His 2017 film A Fantastic Woman, starring Daniela Vega as a transgender woman fighting for dignity after the sudden death of her partner, won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film in 2018 — the first Oscar ever won by a Chilean film.

Lelio went on to direct the English-language films Disobedience (2017) and Gloria Bell (2018), as well as The Wonder (2022) and the musical The Wave (2025), which premiered at the Cannes Film Festival. At the time of his death, he was in the middle of shooting his tenth feature film, Chilean Poet, an adaptation of Alejandro Zambra's novel.

ChileActores, the Chilean actors' organization, called his death "an enormous loss for the culture and the audiovisual sector of our country."

Rest in Peace, Sebastián Lelio.

Sources: Reuters, confirming his death and the family's statement; Emol; CNN Chile; ChileActores.
